lines: Fourteen barrels in the store and every one of them goes out through those posts.
Mirehaven sells me the oil at what it costs them. They have always done that.
A town that does that is a town worth the walk, whatever else you hear about it.
I waded it. Everyone says wade it. I am telling you: go round.
It is not the water. It is that you cannot see the far side while you are in it.
Twenty minutes of dry plank against six minutes of not knowing. Take the twenty.
Emberfall to Mirehaven, three times a week, and half my bag is for one address now.
Not the Hall. Not the town office. A survey camp that was not here last spring.
They have their own seal. A circle with a line through it. You see it everywhere.
Emberfall to Mirehaven and back. Two days if the span were up. Three as it is.
Say what you like about the fog. Nobody has ever robbed me on this road.
You would have to be able to see me first.
